title: A decision, an observation, an outcome or a note
description: Decisions and their reasoning on their way to the record. Any service may publish; `journal listen` is the single writer, which is why this is on the bus at all. Built by journal.bus.to_message from Entry.to_dict.

id.description: **Ignored by the reader, and sent anyway.** It is derived from the content, so the consumer recomputes it locally: a sender cannot claim an id that does not match what it sent, and two services publishing the same decision still collapse to one row. Present because `Entry.to_dict` is the wire format and the record's own format alike.

time.description: Epoch seconds. Part of the content the id is derived from, with actor and title.

kind.description: A decision carries a rationale; an observation is something noticed and not acted on, which is useful as a negative example; an outcome links to an earlier entry by `parent`.

actor.description: Which service or person. Also the bus message's source when publishing.

title.description: The only field without a usable default: `journal.bus.from_message` returns None for an empty one and the entry is dropped.

context.description: The structured record a later study reads. Deliberately open: this is where a service writes what it knew at the time, and pinning its keys here would make every new measurement a change to this contract.

confidence.description: Null rather than absent when unknown, because 0.0 and "not stated" are different claims.

parent.description: The id of the entry this is an outcome of. Empty for entries that are not.
